author: kirubaharan181
description: Plans, approves and verifies releases and deployments. Use when promoting a build to staging or production. Do NOT use for building pipelines.
purpose: Controls how a tested build reaches users: release planning and notes, readiness, change approval, staging and production deployment, migrations, DNS, TLS, load balancing, rollback planning, smoke tests and sign-off. It owns stages 126-139 and never treats an agent as the approver of production changes.
when_to_use: A release needs planning, readiness review or notes.
A build must be deployed to staging or production with verification.
A migration, rollback or cutover plan is needed.
when_not_to_use: Creating the pipeline itself: use devops-platform.
Governing risky production changes in general: use secure-change-control.
Running day-to-day cloud operations: use cloud-hosting-operations.
prerequisites: Test and security sign-off for the build under release.
A named human approver for production.
A tested rollback path and a change window.
No external API keys, paid services or network access are required; work uses files and tools already approved in the repository.
outputs: approval record with a named human

decision_rules.situation: Sign-off is for a different build
decision_rules.action: Stop; require evidence for the candidate.
Block production until one is tested.
Split into expand then contract releases.
Roll back by the plan and record the failure.

examples.title: Readiness review
examples.context: Tests passed on build 2.8.0-rc3; security sign-off references rc2.
examples.behavior: Compare build identifiers across evidence, find the mismatch, and mark readiness BLOCKED until the security evidence matches.
examples.output: Readiness record with BLOCKED status and the missing evidence.
examples.acceptance: No production approval is requested until identifiers match.

examples.title: Plan a safe migration
examples.behavior: Plan expand and contract: add column, backfill in batches, switch reads, then drop later.
examples.output: Two-release migration plan with rollback at each step.
examples.acceptance: Each step is reversible and has a verification query.

limitations: Cannot deploy or approve on its own authority: production needs a named human.
Cannot verify live production without access; it records the checks to run.
Rollback assumes data compatibility has been tested.

troubleshooting.resolution: Do not proceed; reschedule or use the documented delegate.
Fix the check; do not ignore a failure.
Generate from merged changes and have the owner review.

handoffs.artifact: release markers and rollback criteria for monitoring
